display_title: fiberL: Automated Fiber Length and Alignment Measurement from SEM Images
one_liner: A Streamlit tool that traces every fiber in an SEM image of a nanofiber gel and reports length and orientation distributions. It is meant to replace slow, subjective hand-tracing.
problem: Materials researchers characterize electrospun nanofiber gels by hand-tracing fibers in SEM images. That is slow, analyst-dependent, and covers only a few dozen fibers per sample, so comparisons between fabrication conditions are weakly powered.
approach: Perona-Malik anisotropic diffusion, morphological top-hat, fixed threshold combined with Canny edges, and skeletonization. Junctions are found with 17 hit-or-miss kernels. Segments meeting at a junction are paired by most anti-parallel direction and merged with union-find. Arc length, PCA orientation and a tangent-correlation persistence length are then computed per fiber. The interactive app provides crop, scale-bar and parameter controls, plus CSV/PNG/PDF export. Prototyped in the lonespear/aerogel Colab notebooks (2024).
decision_relevance: Turns a manual measurement into a repeatable instrument, so a lab can test whether a fabrication condition (e.g., high-alignment vs 2:1 alignment gels) changes fiber alignment and length, with known measurement error. This is not yet demonstrated: no validation or between-condition comparison exists.

headline_results.claim: End-to-end pipeline implemented: anisotropic diffusion, top-hat, threshold with Canny, skeleton, 17 hit-or-miss junction kernels, direction-based junction pairing, union-find merging, per-fiber length/orientation statistics, CSV/PNG/PDF export.

headline_results.claim: Grew out of 2024 prototype notebooks run on real SEM images of PCL/PLCL nanofiber gels. One preprocessing change cut detected branch points on the same image from 12,832 to 5,702, while mean segment length moved only from 136.4 to 127.7 px.

limitations: No ground truth: never compared against manual tracing, synthetic fibers of known geometry, or an established tool (DiameterJ, FiberApp, ImageJ Ridge Detection).
Physical calibration is collected in the UI but never applied; all outputs are in pixels.

Persistence-length estimator uses exp(-s/Lp) instead of the 2D worm-like-chain form exp(-s/2Lp) and a 20-pixel lag window; in simulation it returns about 2x true Lp and saturates near 140 px on skeleton-like chains.
'Lambda' = log(Lp)/L is not dimensionless and changes with the unit choice.
Arc length on pixel skeletons carries a +3-5% diagonal-step bias; greedy point ordering adds a heavy upper tail (p90 +44-77% for curvy fibers in simulation).
Orientation mean/SD computed linearly on axial (0-180 deg) data; rose diagram is mirrored relative to image coordinates.
Results depend on about 9 hand-set thresholds with no sensitivity analysis; fibers cut by the image border are length-censored; 2D projection understates true length.
Exercised only on a handful of images from one lab; junction pairing is unvalidated at crossings and bundles.

Apply the pixel-to-unit calibration to every length/Lp output (read the TIFF pixel-size tag when present), and fix the app guard so the default number_input value does not count as a completed calibration.
Fix or drop persistence length (2D WLC factor, lag window, sub-pixel centerline) and drop or redefine the lambda coefficient.
Validate: synthetic WLC phantoms (length bias/RMSE, Lp recovery) and manual tracing on 2-3 real images (Bland-Altman, detection precision/recall).
Run a parameter sensitivity screen on the 6 highalign replicate images and report which thresholds move median length and alignment.
Use axial circular statistics for orientation (doubled-angle mean, nematic order parameter) and fix the mirrored rose diagram.

Add a README and LICENSE (account for the embedded GPL-3.0 MedPy anisotropic_diffusion code).
